text.p: Gillette Co President Michael Hawley said on Monday its shareholders approved the company's $7 billion merger with battery-maker Duracell International Inc.
More than 99 percent of Gillette shareholders approved the merger, Hawley said, which will convert each outstanding share of Duracell into 0.904 of one share of Gillette common stock.
Hawley repeated earlier statements that the merger would be immediately accretive to earnings and would result in between $80 million to $120 million in annualized savings.
Hawley said savings between the two company's would be realized by consolidating headquarter functions and sales forces internationally.
Duracell had revenues of $2.3 billion in fiscal 1996.
The merger is expected to be completed at the close of business on December 31 1996.
